base_member_text: [L164-L169] (MED/Fortran-semantics) The claim that post-allocation initialization such as `xyz = 0` is superfluous is unsafe: allocatable numeric arrays are not generally initialized by allocation, so removing it can expose undefined values.
audit_member_text: [L164-L169] (MED/unsafe-initialization-guidance) The recommendation to omit zero initialization provides no requirement that every array element be assigned before use, although allocation alone does not initialize real values.

adversarial.rationale: The complete allocation discussion gives no assignment-before-read condition for omitting initialization, and xyz is only a documentation placeholder, so no caller or initializer supplies a missing guarantee. Some scratch arrays are fully overwritten (for example trunk/src/xbeachlibrary/roelvink.F90:73-84), but that does not justify the unrestricted recommendation; the build flags in trunk/src/xbeachlibrary/Makefile.am:99-105 likewise provide no allocation-time zeroing guarantee. This stands as unsafe documentation guidance, not evidence that an existing execution necessarily reads undefined v

base_member_text: [L139-L162] (MED/Fortran-semantics) The proposed replacement for saved scratch arrays omits a deallocation example and assumes automatic removal at subroutine exit, while the original saved allocation can retain dimensions across calls; callers with changing local-grid sizes therefore lack a safe lifecycle contract.
audit_member_text: [L139-L154] (MED/documented-allocation-limitation) The documented saved scratch-array pattern allocates only once and explicitly leaves wrong-sized arrays possible when subsequent spacepar instances have different dimensions.

adversarial.rationale: The finding treats a deliberately criticized example as the recommended lifecycle: lines 152-154 explicitly warn that SAVE can retain the wrong dimensions, and lines 156-162 replace it with a local allocatable without SAVE. Such a local allocatable is automatically deallocated on procedure exit, so the replacement allocates the current dimensions on each call and needs no explicit deallocation example; the cited passage does not establish a defect in that guidance.

neutralizer.quote:
This solution, however, is not good when one should define more than
one spacepar variable (apart from sglobal and slocal). Then the size
of the 'saved' matrices could be wrong.

I suggest to simply allocate these scratch arrays:

  real*8, dimension(:,:), allocatable :: xyz
  allocate(xyz(s%nx+1,s%ny+1))

According to the fortran95 standard, these allocated arrays are 
automatically removed at the exit of the subroutine.
